stages.title: Supply-side policy: infrastructure and its effects
stages.sub: Explain how improving infrastructure shifts LRAS and evaluate the resulting benefits.

steps.q: A government spends billions building new motorways, ports and broadband networks over ten years. Is this the government using markets and price signals, or stepping in directly to build capacity itself?
steps.right: Stepping in directly to build capacity itself
steps.wrong: Using markets and price signals to encourage firms
steps.hint: Think about who is doing the building here: private firms responding to prices, or the state itself.

steps.hint: You are asking about the economy's productive capacity, not how much people want to buy.

steps.q: After LRAS shifts right, the economy can produce more output year after year without prices rising as fast as before. What has happened to the maximum sustainable rate the economy can grow at?
steps.right: It has risen, without extra inflationary pressure
steps.wrong: It has fallen, causing higher inflation
steps.hint: A bigger productive capacity means more can be produced before shortages push prices up.

steps.q: New infrastructure projects need workers with construction, engineering and digital skills in the regions being built up. What happens to workers who were previously unemployed because their skills or location did not match available jobs?
steps.right: Some can now find work that matches their skills or area
steps.wrong: They remain unemployed regardless of the projects
steps.hint: Structural unemployment happens when skills or location do not match jobs. Does building new capacity in an area change that mismatch?
